title: PR waveform regression detector and multi-slice prober
creator: Lena Zhou
description: Build a CI-side regression detector that treats performance traces as time-series waveforms rather than single-point summaries. The detector will ingest per-request token flow and latency traces from PR-driven benchmark runs, perform slice-aware spectral and shape analysis, and raise deterministic gates when waveform divergence exceeds calibrated thresholds. Goals: 1) reduce false positives from noisy p95 jitter, 2) detect microburst patterns that reduce tokens/sec for specific sequence-length slices, and 3) provide actionable slice-level signals for engineers (example: ‘kv-cache thrash on seq512 causing 18% tokens/sec drop’). The system will integrate with PR gating to block merges for severe regressions and attach diagnostic artifacts to the PR (canonical traces, spectrogram diffs, and representative requests).
acceptance_criteria: PR job produces canonical per-token-flow traces and per-request latency timelines for each benchmark run
Waveform detector computes baseline spectral profile per slice and compares PR run profile to baseline with configurable sensitivity
Detector emits pass/warn/fail decision with a human-readable explanation and top 3 contributing slices
Failure attaches a zipped artifact to the PR with top traces, spectrogram image, and a minimal reproduction script
Average false positive rate on historical CI data < 3% over the last 90 days at default sensitivity
End-to-end CI runtime for detector stage < 12 minutes in our standard PR runner
steps: 1) Extend benchmark harness to record fine-grained token timestamps and per-token latency for streaming tests
2) Implement lightweight trace serializer (binary packed + gzip) to keep artifacts reasonable in size
3) Build waveform preprocessor: normalize traces by sequence length and warmup prefix, compute STFT and key shape features (rise time, plateau, drop events)
4) Define slice keys: model-variant, sequence-length-bucket, batch-size, compilation-kernel-version
5) Compute rolling baseline profiles stored in S3 with TTL and versioning; include bootstrapped confidence intervals
6) Implement comparison rules: spectral KL divergence threshold + shape event count delta + median tokens/sec delta for the slice
7) Wire detector to CI: run after benchmark stage, publish decision as GitHub check with artifact links
8) Add a soft-fail (warn) mode for first 2 weeks of rollout and a replay mode that re-checks against last successful baseline
9) Add dashboard widgets for top failing slices and historical waveform anomaly rate

notes: Implementation trade-offs: keep the detector deterministic and explainable — avoid opaque ML classifiers in the CI gate. Investigate ML-based anomaly scorer as a separate opt-in job.
We should prioritize slices that historically drive customer impact: seq256+, kv-cache enabled, and dedicated-gpu variants.
Fallback behavior: if baseline is missing or low-confidence, detector should return 'no-baseline' and mark job as informational, not a hard block.
Privacy: traces contain no customer text; only timing and token counts. Still run through a lightweight scrubber for any stray metadata before uploading.
